lit-short-01-c2.text: Edgar Allan Poe (1842). Review of Twice-Told Tales (Graham's Magazine, May 1842). Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore.
lit-short-01-c2.quote: the unity of effect or impression is a point of the greatest importance.
lit-short-01-c2.claim: Edgar Allan Poe's principle of the single effect (1842) holds that every element of a story should contribute to one unified emotional impact.

lit-short-03-c1.quote: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov was the author of several hundred works of short fiction and of several plays
lit-short-03-c1.claim: A Russian doctor and writer, he wrote several hundred stories alongside his major plays.

lit-short-02-c2.text: Edgar Allan Poe (1846). The Philosophy of Composition. Edgar Allan Poe Society of Baltimore.
lit-short-02-c2.quote: If any literary work is too long to be read at one sitting, we must be content to dispense with the immensely important effect derivable from unity of impression
lit-short-02-c2.claim: it can be read at one sitting, so the writer can plan a single unified effect on the reader and execute it without interruption.

lit-short-04-c1.text: James Joyce (1906). James Joyce: Quotations, Comments on the Works. Ricorso.
lit-short-04-c1.quote: I have written it for the most part in a style of scrupulous meanness
lit-short-04-c1.claim: The stories are written, Joyce said, in 'a style of scrupulous meanness.'

lit-short-05-c3.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (2013). Press release, Nobel Prize in Literature 2013. NobelPrize.org.
lit-short-05-c3.quote: The Nobel Prize in Literature for 2013 is awarded to the Canadian author Alice Munro
lit-short-05-c3.claim: Alice Munro (1931-2024) is now widely considered the greatest contemporary short-story writer. Canadian, Nobel Prize 2013.
